title: Norway's immigrant-background cultural participation is institutionally uneven: libraries and museums are strong while concerts and theatre lag
source_unit: Statistics Norway, Cultural use by people with an immigrant background 2025
geography: Norway; immigrants and Norwegian-born people with two immigrant parents aged 9 and older

denominator.unit: completed interviews among a gross sample of 2,991 people with an immigrant background aged 9 or older; response rate 44.5 percent

library_visit.unit: percent visiting a public library during the prior year

cinema_visit.unit: percent visiting a cinema during the prior year

museum_visit.unit: percent visiting a museum during the prior year, up from 48 percent in 2023

mechanism.value: The same population can be highly engaged with public-access institutions while showing weaker participation in selected ticketed or event-based forms

observations.method: Statistics Norway's representative cultural-participation survey of people with an immigrant background, with a separate comparison to the total-population Cultural Barometer.
observations.uncertainty: These are cross-sectional self-reports; the report does not identify household income, ticket prices, travel time, language, venue supply, or individual transitions from one institution to another.
observations.subgroup: Immigrants and Norwegian-born people with two immigrant parents, aged 9 or older; the subgroup is not equivalent to all foreign-born residents or all ethnic-minority residents.
observations.counterinterpretation: Library and museum participation may reflect free or publicly supported access, school and family pathways, or local supply rather than a general preference for those institutions over concerts or theatre.

observations.period: 2025 cultural participation survey; immigrant-background versus total-population pattern

denominator.unit: completed immigrant-background interviews; published comparisons use the separate total-population Cultural Barometer as comparator

similar_participation.value: cinema, ballet/dance, festivals, art exhibitions, and opera were attended to a similar extent by people with an immigrant background and the total population

lower_participation.value: the immigrant-background group had a lower share attending theatre performances and concerts than the total population

higher_participation.value: the immigrant-background group visited public libraries and museums more often and attended religious or life-stance meetings more often than the total population

mechanism.value: Cultural inclusion is venue-specific and cannot be reduced to a single assimilation or exclusion score

observations.method: Statistics Norway comparison of 2025 immigrant-background survey estimates with the total-population Cultural Barometer.
observations.uncertainty: The English release summarizes several comparisons without publishing all corresponding point estimates; no causal explanation or adjustment for age, education, income, geography, or household composition is supplied in the release.
observations.subgroup: Immigrants and Norwegian-born people with two immigrant parents compared with the total Norwegian survey population.
observations.counterinterpretation: Observed venue differences may be compositional or opportunity-driven; they do not show cultural preference, discrimination, or institutional quality by themselves.

observations.period: 2025 cultural participation survey; desired additional participation and barriers

denominator.unit: completed immigrant-background interviews; desire shares refer to the relevant activity questions

want_more_cinema.unit: percent wanting to attend cinema more frequently

want_more_concerts.unit: percent wanting to attend concerts more frequently

want_more_museums_theatre.unit: reported share wanting to visit museums and theatres more frequently

barriers.value: lack of time, financial reasons, and lack of an interesting selection were the recurring barriers; younger people more often reported time, adults more often money and selection, and older people more often health

mechanism.value: High desired participation coexists with practical constraints that vary by life stage, so observed attendance is not a clean measure of cultural interest

observations.method: Statistics Norway survey questions on desired additional cultural participation and reasons for not participating more frequently.
observations.uncertainty: The release does not provide full barrier percentages, event prices, travel time, or evidence that stated desire later converted into attendance.
observations.subgroup: Respondents with an immigrant background who answered the relevant participation and desire questions; estimates are not causal effects.
observations.counterinterpretation: Stated desire may include aspirational or socially desirable responses, and an 'interesting selection' barrier may reflect supply mismatch rather than affordability or exclusion.

observations.period: 2025 StatBank table 14638; age-specific barriers for cinema and concerts

denominator.unit: completed immigrant-background interviews; StatBank publishes percentages by age and activity among respondents reporting the relevant reason question

cinema_financial_by_age.unit: percent reporting financial reason for not attending cinema more frequently, by age

cinema_time_by_age.unit: percent reporting lack of time for not attending cinema more frequently, by age

concert_financial_by_age.unit: percent reporting financial reason for not attending concerts more frequently, by age

concert_time_by_age.unit: percent reporting lack of time for not attending concerts more frequently, by age

mechanism.value: The barrier mix changes by life stage: time peaks for working-age concert audiences, while financial barriers are highest among ages 16-44; age-specific access cannot be inferred from a single national barrier average

observations.method: Statistics Norway StatBank table 14638, queried for both sexes, 2025, cinema and concert activities, and financial/time reasons across five age groups.
observations.uncertainty: These are percentages for selected reasons and activities, not mutually exclusive barriers or causal effects; the table does not show income, ticket prices, travel time, household composition, or the number of people in each age-by-activity question base.
observations.subgroup: People with an immigrant background aged 9-15, 16-24, 25-44, 45-66, and 67 years or older; the 9+ subgroup definition follows Statistics Norway.
observations.counterinterpretation: Age differences may reflect life-stage schedules, school or family mediation, health, venue supply, or question interpretation rather than a direct price or time effect.

observations.period: 2025 StatBank table 14637; age-specific realized cultural use

denominator.unit: completed immigrant-background interviews; StatBank publishes annual participation shares by age and activity

cinema_use_by_age.unit: percent visiting a cinema in the prior 12 months, by age

library_use_by_age.unit: percent visiting a public library in the prior 12 months, by age

concert_use_by_age.unit: percent attending a concert in the prior 12 months, by age

theatre_use_by_age.unit: percent attending theatre, musical, or revue in the prior 12 months, by age

mechanism.value: Age-specific realized use does not mirror barriers one-for-one: cinema and theatre are strongly age-graded, while concert participation is comparatively flat despite age-varying financial and time constraints

observations.method: Statistics Norway StatBank table 14637, queried for both sexes, 2025, selected cultural activities, and six age categories.
observations.uncertainty: These are cross-sectional annual participation shares; they do not show visit frequency, price, venue supply, transport, household resources, or the causal pathway from a reported barrier to non-use.
observations.subgroup: People with an immigrant background aged 9-15, 16-24, 25-44, 45-66, and 67 years or older.
observations.counterinterpretation: Age gradients may reflect education, family mediation, cohort tastes, local supply, health, or survey response composition rather than life-stage affordability or time pressure alone.

observations.period: 2021-2025 StatBank table 14637; immigrant-background recovery and venue divergence

denominator.unit: 2025 completed immigrant-background interviews; table supplies comparable published shares for the 2021, 2023, and 2025 waves

cinema_series.unit: percent visiting cinema in prior 12 months

library_series.unit: percent visiting public library in prior 12 months

museum_series.unit: percent visiting museum in prior 12 months

concert_series.unit: percent attending concert in prior 12 months

theatre_series.unit: percent attending theatre, musical, or revue in prior 12 months

mechanism.value: Recovery after 2021 was broad but not identical: libraries and museums continued rising through 2025, while cinema and concerts eased after 2023 and theatre remained much lower than the other venues

observations.method: Statistics Norway StatBank table 14637, queried for both sexes, all ages, selected activities, and the 2021, 2023, and 2025 survey years.
observations.uncertainty: These are repeated cross-sectional estimates, not a panel; changes may reflect restrictions, questionnaire conditions, venue supply, cohort composition, or sampling variation, and they do not establish individual persistence or causal recovery.
observations.subgroup: People with an immigrant background aged 9 or older; the subgroup sample and survey context are documented by Statistics Norway.
observations.counterinterpretation: The post-2021 increases may largely represent reopening and normalization rather than a durable cultural transformation; the 2025 easing in cinema and concerts may be ordinary year-to-year variation.

related_sources.claim: Statistics Norway's StatBank lists tables 14636-14638 for immigrant-background cultural participation, subgroup use, and barriers from 2021 through 2025.
StatBank table 14638 provides official 2025 age-specific percentages for financial and time barriers by cultural activity among people with an immigrant background.
StatBank table 14637 provides official 2025 age-specific participation shares and average visits by cultural activity among people with an immigrant background.
The companion total-population Cultural Barometer supplies the comparison population and repeated cultural-participation context.

boundary: This record adds subgroup-specific cultural participation, unmet demand, and barrier evidence from Norway. It does not establish assimilation, discrimination, causal access barriers, cultural preference, household welfare, or individual-level persistence.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Statistics Norway's English report page, linked 2025 immigrant-background report, and StatBank cultural-barometer table index were reviewed for the sample, subgroup definition, participation comparisons, desired-use shares, barriers, and available machine-readable tables.
